stem: Kavya compares older numeral systems with the Hindu number system used today.

parts.text: Which claim states what makes the Hindu number system efficient?

options.text: Ten digits $0$–$9$, base-$10$ place value, and zero as both a digit and a number.
Call the answer digits $0$–$9$ only, with no place value and no role for zero.
Place value is what creates the ten digits, so the digits come after places are named.

parts.text: Give one reason for your choice.

part_answers.answer: Compact writing needs all three together: ten digits, base-10 places, and zero filling empty places and naming the number zero.

teacher.key_rationale: Efficiency needs digits 0–9, place value, and zero as digit and number together. Digits alone omit place value and zero. Reversing so place value creates digits flips the relation.
